claim: Population averaging due to paracrine communication can arbitrarily reduce cellular response variability.
source: Population averaging due to paracrine communication can arbitrarily reduce cellular response variability.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement presented in the abstract about the potential of paracrine communication.

claim: Paracrine communication reduces gradient noise but also reduces the gradient magnitude.
source: We find that while paracrine communication reduces gradient noise, it also reduces the gradient magnitude.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements and computational analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: There exists a maximum gradient signal to noise ratio in paracrine communication.
source: Accordingly we predict the existence of a maximum gradient signal to noise ratio.
evidence: This prediction is based on computational modeling and analysis of Ca2+ and ERK gradients.

claim: Cells utilize optimal levels of paracrine signaling to maximize the accuracy of gradient-based positional information.
source: Direct in vitro measurement of paracrine communication verifies these predictions and reveals that cells utilize optimal levels of paracrine signaling to maximize the accuracy of gradient-based positional information.
evidence: This is supported by direct measurements using the DREADD system and comparison with predicted optimal PCD.

claim: Single-cell quantification shows that the concentration of many signaling molecules can vary by approximately 25% (coefficient of variation).
source: For instance, single-cell quantification of protein concentration variability between cells shows that the concentration of many signaling molecules can vary by ∼25% (coefficient of variation) (Sigal et al., 2006; Bar-Even et al., 2006; Spencer et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Single-molecule kinetics regulates gene expression and is an inherently stochastic process.
source: Notably, single-molecule kinetics regulates gene expression and, as a result, is an inherently stochastic process (Sanchez and Golding, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Response variability potentially degrades transmitted information and decreases downstream effector ability to reliably respond to environmental changes.
source: Response variability potentially degrades transmitted information and decreases downstream effector ability to reliably respond to environmental changes (Selimkhanov et al., 2014; Cheong et al., 2011; Voliotis et al., 2014; Hansen and O'Shea, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Single-cell noise in NFκB dynamics creates robust population level responses to a wider range of inputs.
source: For example, single-cell noise in NFκB dynamics creates robust population level responses to a wider range of inputs (Hughey et al., 2014; Kellogg and Tay, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Paracrine signaling averaging functions such that the local concentration of the paracrine ligand is the average ligand concentration secreted by local cells.
source: Specifically, paracrine signaling averaging functions such that the local concentration of the paracrine ligand, or the concentration of ligand a cell is exposed to, is the average ligand concentration secreted by local cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a mechanistic description supported by the model presented in Figure 1A.

claim: Paracrine communication increases post-paracrine cellular response fidelity.
source: Indeed, the benefits from paracrine communication were previously demonstrated to increase post-paracrine cellular response fidelity (Rand et al., 2012; Shalek et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ATP activates ERK in a paracrine fashion in MCF-10A cells.
source: ATP activates ERK in a paracrine fashion in MCF-10A cells.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In MCF-10A cells, addition of extracellular ATP increases ERK kinase activity in an EGFR dependent manner.
source: In the mammary epithelial cell line MCF-10A, addition of extracellular ATP increases ERK kinase activity in an EGFR dependent manner (Figure 1B) similar to results reported in other in vitro epithelial models (Yin et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1B and citation to previous work.

claim: Inhibiting EGFR with tryphostin AG1478 prevents ERK activation upon ATP addition.
source: Inhibiting EGFR with tryphostin AG1478 prevents ERK activation upon ATP addition showing that ERK activation depends on secreted EGF binding to EGFR (Wetzker and Böhmer, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation.

claim: ERK response variability within clusters decreases with increasing cluster density.
source: ERK response variability within clusters decreases with increasing cluster density indicating increased intercellular communication ability.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the clustering analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Increased intercellular communication ability is not observed in the absence of paracrine communication such as with the primary Ca2+ response to ATP.
source: Increased intercellular communication ability is not observed in the absence of paracrine communication such as with the primary Ca2+ response to ATP (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Disrupting paracrine communication by partially inhibiting Src results in the loss of the observed benefit of paracrine communication in higher density clusters.
source: Furthermore, disrupting paracrine communication by partially inhibiting Src results in the loss of the observed benefit of paracrine communication in higher density clusters (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplements 3,4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Paracrine averaging using a PCD of 100 μm increases response SNR from 0.9 to 20.2 by decreasing noise of the predicted ERK response.
source: This analysis indicates that paracrine averaging using a PCD of 100 μm increases response SNR from 0.9 to 20.2 by decreasing noise, or response variability, of the predicted ERK response (Figure 1E, gray/black).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of experimental Ca2+ data.

claim: The overall response SNR can increase up to eightyfold at PCDs of 500 μm when paracrine diffusion is not limiting.
source: Interestingly, our analysis estimates that the overall response SNR can increase up to eightyfold at PCDs of 500 μm when paracrine diffusion is not limiting, and up to twenty fivefold when diffusion of the paracrine ligand is limiting (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Extracellular ATP released from necrotic cells act as DAMPs to activate healthy cells proximal to the wound.
source: Extracellular ATP released from necrotic cells act as DAMPs to activate healthy cells proximal to the wound (Cordeiro and Jacinto, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Wounding in the presence of apyrase inhibits both Ca2+ and ERK response.
source: We verified the key role of ATP in initial wound response by wounding in the presence of apyrase, an enzyme that rapidly hydrolyzes ATP. Wounding in the presence of apyrase inhibits both Ca2+ and ERK response (Figure 2D,E, insets).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E insets.

claim: The CV for Ca2+ wound response shows statistically higher variability than ERK wound response.
source: Indeed, the CV for Ca2+ wound response shows statistically higher variability than ERK wound response indicating that paracrine communication reduces response variability during initial wound response.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The maximal increase of cellular response fidelity occurs at a PCD of approximately 100 μm, or approximately 3 cell diameters.
source: The maximal increase of cellular response fidelity occurrs at a PCD of ∼100 μm, or approximately 3 cell diameters.
evidence: This is based on SNR analysis of wound response data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The predicted PCD with maximal benefit is 91.0+/-6.3 μm (SEM, N = 5).
source: The difference in rates at which the signal and noise decrease results in a maximum SNR at a PCD of 91.0+/-6.3 μm (SEM, N = 5) (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of wound response data.

claim: CNO addition selectively activates Ca2+ response in DREADD expressing cells while the surrounding non-expressing cells show no response.
source: CNO addition selectively activates Ca2+ response in DREADD expressing cells while the surrounding non-expressing cells show no response indicating a lack of paracrine activation of Ca2+ response in cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: ERK response was found in both DREADD expressing and the surrounding non-expressing cells upon CNO addition but was inhibited in both cell types in the presence of the EGFR inhibitor tryphosphitin AG1478.
source: Alternatively, ERK response was found in both DREADD expressing and the surrounding non-expressing cells upon CNO addition but was inhibited in both cell types in the presence of the EGFR inhibitor tryphosphitin AG1478, confirming paracrine activation of ERK in the DREADD system (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The paracrine activation of ERK has a communication distance of 99.5+/-19.6 μm (SEM, N = 12 DREADD cells).
source: According to our fit, the paracrine activation of ERK has a communication distance of 99.5+/-19.6 μm (SEM, N = 12 DREADD cells).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements using the DREADD system shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The empirically measured PCD value is statistically similar to the predicted communication distance value that maximizes the SNR of wound response.
source: This empirically measured value is statistically similar to the predicted communication distance value that maximizes the SNR of wound response (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of experimental and computational results shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The cellular communication distance is tuned to maximize the overall response fidelity during wound response signaling.
source: In other words, the cellular communication distance is tuned to maximize the overall response fidelity during wound response signaling.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the agreement between predicted optimal PCD and measured PCD.

claim: In vivo work measuring ERK propagation using the same EKAREV FRET sensor showed propagation extending approximately 100 μm.
source: In vivo work measuring ERK propagation using the same EKAREV FRET sensor also showed propagation extending ∼100 μm (Hiratsuka et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous in vivo work.

claim: Intercellular communication during the initial wound response is optimized to increase overall response fidelity.
source: Our results demonstrate that intercellular communication during the initial wound response is optimized to increase overall response fidelity and provides the initial evidence that matching the wound response to wound damage is a critical aspect to wound healing programs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental and computational results presented.

claim: Paracrine communication increases the fidelity of response at the single-cell level by mitigating biological noise at the single-cell level.
source: Paracrine communication increases the fidelity of response at the single-cell level by mitigating biological noise at the single-cell level.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the results presented.

claim: Each cell integrates information from its local neighborhood to increase its individual response fidelity.
source: Each cell integrates information from its local neighborhood to increase its individual response fidelity.
evidence: This is a mechanistic description of how paracrine communication works based on the model and data.

claim: In vivo studies of ERK response in mammary tumor cells using the same EKAREV FRET sensor show highly variable ERK response that may lead to the survival and propagation of cancer cells.
source: In vivo studies of ERK response in mammary tumor cells using the same EKAREV FRET sensor utilized here show highly variable ERK response that may lead to the survival and propagation of cancer cells (Kumagai et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: One possible mechanism for heterogeneity in tumor cells may be the breakdown of paracrine communication between cells.
source: Although the cause for this heterogeneity is unknown, one possible mechanism may be the breakdown of paracrine communication between cells similar to how our partial inhibition of paracrine communication showed no decrease in ERK variability (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results.

claim: The optimal PCD identified is not universal and depends on the specific shape of the spatial pattern of the initial activating ligand and the noise pattern of the primary response.
source: The optimal PCD we identified is not universal. Rather, the optimal distance depends on the specific shape of the spatial pattern of the initial activating ligand and the noise pattern of the primary response.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis and discussion of the results.

claim: Propagation patterns of the same activating ligand can depend on the physiological signaling context as demonstrated by differences found during in vivo ERK propagations under wound and normal conditions.
source: Additionally, propagation patterns of the same activating ligand can depend on the physiological signaling context as demonstrated by differences found during in vivo ERK propagations under wound and normal conditions (Hiratsuka et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The diffusion coefficients of paracrine signaling molecules can vary by two orders of magnitude.
source: The diffusion coefficients of paracrine signaling molecules can vary by two orders of magnitude, let alone differences in signal strength and receptor sensitivity in individual paracrine signaling pathways (Kreuz et al., 1965; Gregor et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Standard deviation of ERK response per cluster to 10 μM ATP decreases with increasing cluster density (p-value <0.05, Pearson correlation).
source: Standard deviation of ERK response per cluster to 10 μM ATP. Standard deviation decreases with increasing cluster density (p-value <0.05, Pearson correlation).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The standard deviation of Ca2+ response to each ATP dosage is large when compared to the increase in average response with increasing ATP dose (SNR = 0.9).
source: The standard deviation, that is noise, of the Ca2+ response to each ATP dosage is large when compared to the increase in average response with increasing ATP dose, that is signal (SNR = 0.9, gray error bars [standard deviation]).
evidence: This is based on SNR analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Noise decreases when Ca2+ response is locally averaged with a PCD of 100 μm (SNR = 20.2).
source: Noise decreases when Ca2+ response is locally averaged with a PCD of 100 μm (SNR = 20.2, black error bars [standard deviation]).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Variability between cells in the predicted ERK response decreases with increasing PCD.
source: Variability between cells in the predicted ERK response decreases with increasing PCD.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the computational analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The SNR of the predicted ERK response from locally averaged Ca2+ data continually increases with increasing PCD for a model with rapid diffusion.
source: The SNR of the predicted ERK response from locally averaged Ca2+ data continually increases with increasing PCD shown for a model with rapid diffusion (green) or limited by the diffusion rates and integration time of paracrine signals (blue, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The maximum activity per cell shows a larger response in cells closer to the wound compared to cells farther away from the wound for both Ca2+ and ERK.
source: Notably, the maximum activity per cell shows a larger response in cells closer to the wound compared to cells farther away from the wound for both Ca2+ and ERK.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Response gradients demonstrate the importance of the cellular position to determine the cellular response, or positional information.
source: These response gradients demonstrate the importance of the cellular position to determine the cellular response, or positional information (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Locally averaging the cellular Ca2+ response creates a smoother predicted ERK response pattern versus distance from the wound.
source: Locally averaging the cellular Ca2+ response creates a smoother predicted ERK response pattern versus distance from the wound (Figure 3C, gray).
evidence: This is demonstrated by computational analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The reduction in variability also decreases the overall response pattern trend.
source: However, the reduction in variability also decreases the overall response pattern trend.
evidence: This is an observation from the computational analysis.

claim: Locally averaging the Ca2+ signal using increasing PCDs decreases the magnitude of change of the average predicted ERK response between cells closest to the wound and farthest from the wound.
source: Locally averaging the Ca2+ signal using increasing PCDs decreases the magnitude of change of the average predicted ERK response between cells closest to the wound and farthest from the wound (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by computational analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The increase in PCD decreases response noise, but the corresponding decrease in signal demonstrates the limit of PCD on the SNR benefit.
source: Therefore, although the increase in PCD decreases response noise, the corresponding decrease in signal demonstrates the limit of PCD on the SNR benefit (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The predicted PCD with maximal benefit did not change when the model was expanded to consider limitations due to diffusion.
source: The predicted PCD with maximal benefit did not change when we expand the model to consider limitations due to diffusion (Figure 3F green curve, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Mutual information analysis shows a similar PCD with the maximal mutual information at the distance that showed maximal SNR.
source: Similar analysis using mutual information statistics shows a similar PCD with the maximal mutual information at the distance that showed maximal SNR (Figure 3E,F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on mutual information analysis shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The Gq human muscarinic derived GPCR DREADD is activated by a synthetic small molecule, clozapine-N-oxide (CNO), that has no known endogenous receptors.
source: The Gq human muscarinic derived GPCR DREADD is activated by a synthetic small molecule, clozapine-N-oxide (CNO), that has no known endogenous receptors (Armbruster et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: DREADD activates the Gq pathway similar to purinergic ATP receptors.
source: In addition, DREADD activates the Gq pathway similar to purinergic ATP receptors (Dong et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Ca2+ response can propagate from cell-to-cell through gap junctions in some systems.
source: Although some systems show that Ca2+ response can propagate from cell-to-cell through gap junctions (Ross 2012), this does not appear to be the case in MCF-10A cells as non-expressing cells showed no cytosolic Ca2+ increase upon activation of DREADD cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and experimental observation.

claim: Local averaging takes place only at the EGF level between Ca2+ and ERK response in the DREADD system.
source: The Ca2+ and ERK responses in the DREADD system suggest that local averaging takes place only at the EGF level between Ca2+ and ERK response.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results with the DREADD system.

claim: Increasing the ratio of DREADD cells to non-expressing cells shows an increasing ERK response magnitude in non-expressing cells.
source: Additionally, increasing the ratio of DREADD cells to non-expressing cells shows an increasing ERK response magnitude in non-expressing cells, further supporting that paracrine communication locally activates ERK (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: ERK response as a function of distance follows a Gaussian fit, consistent with how the concentration of diffusing molecules changes over distance.
source: ERK response as a function of distance follows a Gaussian fit, consistent with how the concentration of diffusing molecules, like in paracrine signaling, changes over distance (Figure 4E) (Berg, 1993).
evidence: This is based on experimental data and citation to theoretical work.

claim: The PCD was determined by calculating the spread, or sigma, of the Gaussian curve fit to ERK response versus distance.
source: The PCD was determined by calculating the spread, or sigma, of this Gaussian curve.
evidence: This describes the method used to calculate PCD from experimental data.

claim: Cells could potentially take advantage of large PCDs to substantially mitigate biochemical noise under spatially uniform input conditions.
source: Therefore cells could potentially take advantage of large PCDs to substantially mitigate biochemical noise.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion based on the analysis of spatially uniform inputs.

claim: A spatially uniform input, while common in cell culture experiments, is likely an inadequate representation of physiological conditions.
source: However, a spatially uniform input, while common in cell culture experiments, is likely an inadequate representation of physiological conditions.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of experimental conditions.

claim: An extracellular input ligand conveys positional information in wound response similar to developmental systems.
source: Similar to developmental systems, an extracellular input ligand conveys positional information in wound response (Dubuis et al., 2013; Sonnemann and Bement, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Empirical measurements of paracrine communication match the physiologically relevant spatial wound response maximum communication distance.
source: Furthermore, empirical measurements of paracrine communication match the physiologically relevant spatial wound response maximum communication distance.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of experimental and computational results.

claim: The initial steps of wound healing programs propagate information concerning the wound in a manner that is appropriate to the magnitude of damage.
source: The initial steps of wound healing programs propagate information concerning the wound in a manner that is appropriate to the magnitude of damage.
evidence: This is a general statement about wound healing based on the results.

claim: Both inflammatory and fibrotic processes are damaging when they go awry.
source: Both inflammatory and fibrotic processes, critical steps in wound response signaling, are damaging when they go awry.
evidence: This is general knowledge about wound healing processes.

claim: The initial cellular responses and the establishment of signaling gradients are key steps in wound healing.
source: Therefore, the initial cellular responses and the establishment of signaling gradients are key steps in wound healing.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the discussion of wound healing.

claim: The mechanistic details underlying how tissues robustly match the wound response magnitude to the extent of wound-induced damage remain unknown.
source: The mechanistic details underlying how tissues robustly match the wound response magnitude to the extent of wound-induced damage remain unknown.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Matching the wound response to wound damage is a critical aspect to wound healing programs.
source: Our results demonstrate that intercellular communication during the initial wound response is optimized to increase overall response fidelity and provides the initial evidence that matching the wound response to wound damage is a critical aspect to wound healing programs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: Local averaging at the cellular level is a distinct mechanism compared to the benefit of global averaging at the population level.
source: Local averaging at the cellular level is a distinct mechanism compared to the benefit of global averaging at the population level.
evidence: This is a conceptual distinction made in the discussion.

claim: Without any paracrine communication, the reliability of the average of a cell population response can only increase with the size of the population.
source: Without any paracrine communication, the reliability of the average of a cell population response can only increase with the size of the population.
evidence: This is based on statistical principles (central limit theorem).

claim: The increase in reliability from population averaging is only true for the population average and not for individual cells in the population.
source: This is a consequence of the central limit theorem where the uncertainty of a sample average decreases with sample size. However, this increase in reliability is only true for the population average and not for individual cells in the population.
evidence: This is based on statistical principles.

claim: When biologically significant output requires single-cell action, local information sharing via paracrine communication increases cellular response fidelity.
source: However, when biologically significant output requires single-cell action, local information sharing via paracrine communication increases cellular response fidelity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis and discussion.

claim: Whether paracrine communication is required remains context dependent.
source: Therefore, whether paracrine communication is required remains context dependent.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the discussion of different scenarios.

claim: Paracrine information sharing may be more prevalent in signaling networks that support individual cellular decisions and less prevalent in cases where biologically meaningful outcomes result from population averages.
source: It is possible that paracrine information sharing is more prevalent in signaling networks that support individual cellular decisions and less prevalent in cases where biologically meaningful outcomes result from population averages.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the discussion.

claim: The abundance of paracrine communication in mammals demonstrates the heavy utilization of intercellular communication.
source: The abundance of paracrine communication in mammals, that is the activation of a receptor by a ligand synthesized by another cell, demonstrates the heavy utilization of intercellular communication (Ben-Shlomo et al., 2003; 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Theoretical and empirical work in humans and animal collectives has shown that the benefit of collective decision making depends on the size of the group.
source: Theoretical and empirical work in humans and animal collectives has shown that the benefit of collective decision making depends on the size of the group; big crowds are not always better than small crowds (Sasaki et al., 2013; Kao et al., 2014; Hoare et al., 2004; Sueur et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The extent of secretion of each paracrine ligand is likely adjusted to the level of cellular information sharing to ensure an effective collective decision.
source: Therefore, it is likely that the extent of secretion of each paracrine ligand is adjusted to the level of cellular information sharing to ensure an effective collective decision.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the discussion.

claim: The effective PCD can be regulated at the cellular level by several possible factors to optimize the benefit of paracrine communication to the specific noise and spatial patterns characteristic to each signaling system.
source: The effective PCD can be regulated at the cellular level by several possible factors to optimize the benefit of paracrine communication to the specific noise and spatial patterns characteristic to each signaling system (Batsilas et al., 2003; Muratov and Shvartsman, 2003a; 2003b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: PCD depends on the effective diffusion coefficient of the secreted molecule, transmitted signal strength, and receiver cell sensitivity.
source: PCD also depends on the effective diffusion coefficient of the secreted molecule, transmitted signal strength (e.g. number of secreted molecules), and receiver cell sensitivity (e.g. receptor Kd).
evidence: This is based on the theoretical analysis presented in Materials and methods.

claim: Fine-tuning each of these factors provides a possible mechanism for cells to regulate the PCD and thereby the extent a cell locally communicates.
source: Fine-tuning each of these factors provides a possible mechanism for cells to regulate the PCD and thereby the extent a cell locally communicates.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the discussion.

claim: The ability to specifically tune PCD raises the possibility that evolutionary pressures can tune paracrine communication to provide the optimal benefit in many other paracrine communication systems.
source: The ability to specifically tune PCD raises the possibility that evolutionary pressures can tune paracrine communication to provide the optimal benefit in many other paracrine communication systems.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about evolutionary implications.

claim: H2O2 has a diffusion coefficient of approximately 2000 μm2/s.
source: Interestingly, H2O2, another key paracrine signaling molecule critical to initial wound response signaling, has a diffusion coefficient of ∼2000 μm2/s.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the diffusion coefficient of H2O2.

claim: A larger diffusion coefficient could allow for a much longer PCD with reasonable biological integration times.
source: A larger diffusion coefficient could allow for a much longer PCD with reasonable biological integration times.
evidence: This is based on the theoretical analysis of diffusion and integration time.

claim: For diffusion coefficient values of approximately 10–100 μm2/s and a PCD of 100 μm, integration times ranged between 0.5 to 5 min.
source: For diffusion coefficient values of ∼10–100 μm2/s and a PCD of 100 μm (similar to the distance measured in Figure 3) integration times ranged between 0.5 to 5 min.
evidence: This is based on theoretical calculations presented in Materials and methods.

claim: ERK activation is observed only after 5 min post-activation.
source: Given that ERK activation is observed only after 5 min post-activation, the required integration time does not pose an issue.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The extracellular environment is characterized by a low Reynold's number and there is effectively no turbulent mixing in biologically relevant parameters.
source: Since the extracellular environment is characterized by a low Reynold's number there is effectively no turbulent mixing in biologically relevant parameters.
evidence: This is based on fluid dynamics principles.

claim: For paracrine ligands with a diffusion coefficient >40 μm2/sec, advection will have little effect on positional accuracy of initial wound response signaling.
source: This shows that for paracrine ligands with a diffusion coefficient >40 μm2/sec, advection will have little effect on positional accuracy of initial wound response signaling.
evidence: This is based on theoretical analysis of advection effects presented in Materials and methods.
